# Add an API test

`support/core/Api.ts` calls the site's API without the page (`cy.request`) and checks what comes back.
Use it when a story is about data rather than a page ("the products list returns at least one item",
"an unknown id answers 404"), or to check fast what a page test would check slowly.

```ts
it('the products list answers', { tags: ['smoke'] }, () => {
  Api.site().get('/api/products').then((a) =>
    Api.expect(a).status(200).json('items[0].name').fasterThan(2000));
});

it('an unknown product is not found', () => {
  Api.site().get('/api/products/999999').then((a) => Api.expect(a).status(404));
});
```

- **The address:** `Api.site()` is the site under test (baseUrl, as every page test); a path is enough.
  `Api.at('https://api.example.com')` for an API on another host: a client sends its headers (a token, an account)
  only to its own origin, so `Api.site().get('https://other.example/x')` is refused, and a redirect it follows to
  another origin goes on without them (all but Accept and User-Agent).
- **The checks:** `status`, `json(path)` (the field is there), `json(path, value)`, `fasterThan(ms)`;
  the answer's `body` to read it yourself. A path reads `items[0].name`, `total`, `[2].id`. Each check
  fails saying what was asked, what was expected and the answer.
- **Signed in:** `.asRole('user')` sends that role's account from secrets/ (read in Node, never
  logged); `.bearer(token)` a token from `SiteConfig.secret('apiToken')`. **Never a literal password or
  token in the code.**
- **What changes data** (`post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`) runs only against a test environment, never
  the live site, as a form that sends (forms-and-test-data.md).
- **Its family:** `tags: ['smoke']` if a broken API should stop a merge first; one of your own
  otherwise (cypress/families.txt says how). Each call is a step in the test's log.
- **Its time:** every call is timed, yours too: cypress/timings/api.csv, a call much slower than in the previous
  run or past its slow line (cypress.config.ts) listed at the run's end. `--expose apiBudget=1.5` fails any call over 1.5 s;
  `fasterThan(ms)` holds one call to a time of its own.
